input: nums is a list of n integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Values may repeat and input order is significant. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The length of the longest contiguous strictly increasing run in nums. Equal adjacent values break the run. Empty input returns 0. This is not the length of a noncontiguous increasing subsequence.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only the current run length and maximum are retained.
numeric: Input values are compared but never subtracted or arithmetically changed, so the full safe-integer value range is accepted. Indices and run lengths are nonnegative exact integers bounded by n.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Each value either extends the previous strictly increasing contiguous run or starts a new singleton run. No sorting, set, input copy or subsequence DP is used.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 349 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs. TreeNode, where used, is an explicit caller-owned input shape and no node is constructed. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source; method-style interface parity with frozen sources remains unqualified.
